headline: PAGASA Keeps Metro Manila and Broad Areas of Luzon Under Red Rainfall Warning
seoTitle: PAGASA Keeps Red Rainfall Warning Across Luzon | FMB News
seoDescription: PAGASA's 5 p.m. warning placed Metro Manila and broad areas of Luzon under the Red level as the Habagat raised serious flooding risks on August 29.
keywords: Habagat Red warning Metro Manila Luzon
deck: The 5 p.m. warning placed Metro Manila, eight provinces and parts of Batangas under the highest rainfall-warning level as the Habagat continued to affect Luzon and the Visayas.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: PAGASA's Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 17 placed Zambales, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bataan, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Rizal and Cavite under the Red level at 5 p.m. Saturday, August 29. The Red warning also covered Nasugbu, Lian, Tuy, Balayan and Calatagan in Batangas.

PAGASA said serious flooding was expected in flood-prone areas under the Red level. Nueva Ecija, Laguna and other specified Batangas areas were under Orange, while specified parts of Quezon and Batangas were under Yellow.

sections.heading: Weather systems
paragraphs: PAGASA identified the Southwest Monsoon or Habagat as the weather system behind the warning. Its 4 p.m. national forecast said the Habagat was affecting Luzon and the Visayas; the updated synopsis no longer listed a low-pressure area.
The forecast called for heavy to intense monsoon rains over Metro Manila and parts of northern, central and southern Luzon, with possible flash floods or landslides.

sections.heading: Habagat remains a concern
paragraphs: Moderate to strong southwesterly winds were forecast over Luzon, with moderate to rough coastal waters of 1.5 to 3.4 meters.
Rainfall-warning boundaries can change within hours. Residents should use the latest regional warning for immediate decisions rather than relying on an earlier province list.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: This update replaces a duplicate weather route created from the same bulletin and keeps the developing event on FMB News' established canonical route.
Claims in the emailed brief about forced evacuations, relief-stock figures and ferry suspensions were not included because they were not established by the cited PAGASA warning and forecast.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Repeated rain can quickly worsen flooding and slope instability. Communities near rivers, drainage channels and steep terrain should follow evacuation, road-closure and safety instructions from local disaster authorities.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Residents should follow the latest PAGASA rainfall warnings and local disaster advisories because warning levels and covered locations may change at the next issuance.
